text:
maria_dev: quick Q — trying to make our server-side SDK mint service-account JWTs for customers that have multiple orgs/projects. we cache the signed JWT (short TTL) and exchange it for an access token per-request. intermittently some requests to project B get 401s even though project A calls are fine. anyone seen this?

maria_dev: code (node):
```js
const jwt = createSignedJwt({iss: SA_KEY, sub: saEmail, aud: 'https://auth.redwood.ai/token', scope: 'inference.read', exp: Math.floor(Date.now()/1000) + 300});
const token = await exchangeJwtForToken(jwt, {project: projectId}); // we cache `jwt` by saEmail
```

maria_dev: we're basically reusing the exact same signed JWT for requests across orgs if the SA is shared. is the audience/scoping causing the token exchange to be invalid for some projects? @kai_sdk any SDK pitfalls here? :thinking_face:

kai_sdk: short answer: yes, audience and audience-scoped restrictions can bite here. if the token exchange service validates that the JWT was minted for a specific project audience (or the exchange binds the resulting access token to a project), reusing the same JWT across projects can fail. also check the `aud` and any `project` claim you might be adding.

kai_sdk: longer: the signed JWT (the assertion) is presented to the token endpoint. the token endpoint may also require a `target_project` param or check `sub` vs allowed projects for that SA. caching only the raw signed JWT keyed by saEmail is risky — include the target project/org in the cache key.

kai_sdk: suggest change: cache by `${saEmail}::${aud}::${projectId}` and set TTL to something slightly less than the `exp`. if you're minting 5m JWTs, exchange immediately rather than reuse across different audiences.

olivia_sec: fwiw from a security perspective: prefer minting short-lived assertions (<=5m) and don't persist private keys in plain disk. use KMS/HSM to sign if possible. also minimize scopes in the JWT (least privilege). rotate SA keys regularly.

sam_platform: another gotcha: if project B has a policy that requires an additional claim (e.g., `x-org-id`) you won't see it unless you explicitly include it in the assertion. token service logs usually show which claim check failed — look there.

maria_dev: that makes sense. so do we recommend the SDK perform the exchange for the caller (i.e., accept project param and return access token) rather than exposing signed JWT caching to callers?

kai_sdk: yes, for dev ergonomics and to avoid misuse. SDK should provide a helper `getAccessTokenForProject(saKey, saEmail, projectId)` that internally signs + exchanges and caches the final access token keyed by (saEmail, projectId, scopes). caching the exchanged access token is safer because the token endpoint already scoped it correctly.

kai_sdk: note: access tokens may be longer lived than assertions — validate `exp` on the access token and refresh proactively. also handle 401 by retrying the exchange once (to avoid stuck caches).

olivia_sec: add: when implementing retry, rate-limit retries and emit audit events so we can see repeated failures (possible compromised key).

maria_dev: nice. i'll change the cache key first and then switch to caching access tokens.

docs-bot: FYI docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/auth/service-accounts#jwt-exchange (added a short example for per-project caches) :book: :white_check_mark:

maria_dev: thanks all — i'll open a tiny PR tomorrow to update client helper and add tests for two-project flows. :rocket:
